payload.goal:
Add order priority and backorders to this warehouse codebase, across every layer that already exists.

Domain  - src/domain/orders.ts:
- Export type OrderPriority = "standard" | "express".
- Order gains a readonly priority field of that type. It is optional at the call site: an order placed without a priority is treated as "standard", so existing callers keep working unchanged.
- placeOrder throws OrderError when a priority is supplied and is neither "standard" nor "express".
- Export interface Backorder with readonly orderId, skuId and missing fields, where missing is a positive integer.
- WarehouseState gains a readonly backorders field keyed by order id.
- reserveOrder records a Backorder for every line whose quantity exceeds the available units, instead of throwing, and leaves the order in a status from which it can still be cancelled.
- Export listBackorders(state) returning every recorded Backorder.

Application  - src/application/warehouse-service.ts:
- The service exposes the new operations and emits a warehouse event for a recorded backorder.

Fulfillment  - src/fulfillment/planner.ts:
- Within one wave, planFulfillment lists express orders before standard ones. Its existing signature does not change.

Durability  - src/durability/journal.ts:
- HistoryAnalytics gains a backorders count derived from the events.

API  - src/api/server.ts:
- The server exposes the backorders of the current state.

Presentation  - src/presentation/tower.ts:
- The rendered SVG distinguishes express orders from standard ones.

Probe  - src/probe/g6.ts and a package script named study:g6-probe:
- Follow the shape of the existing probes: export main() returning a JSON string, and write exactly one JSON object to stdout when invoked directly, with no other output.
- Two invocations from the same commit must emit byte-identical output.

Preserve all existing behaviour and keep every existing test passing. Put new tests next to the code they cover, inside the directories the test script already scans.

scripts.test: node --test src/domain/*.test.ts src/probe/*.test.ts src/scenarios/*.test.ts src/application/*.test.ts src/presentation/*.test.ts src/api/*.test.ts src/fulfillment/*.test.ts src/durability/*.test.ts

root.title: Warehouse order priority and backorders
root.objective: Add order priority and backorders across the warehouse stack while preserving existing behavior.
expectedOutcomes: The domain model supports optional order priority, backorder recording, and backorder listing.
The existing layers consume the new domain contract without regressing current behavior.
The probe path and package script produce stable, single-object JSON output.

complexitySignals.rationale: This is a cross-layer contract change spanning domain rules, service orchestration, fulfillment ordering, persistence analytics, external surfaces, and a new deterministic probe.

cut.rationale: The work decomposes cleanly along existing layer boundaries, but the shared order/backorder semantics must remain consistent across all of them.

children.title: Domain order contract
children.objective: Extend the order domain with optional priority, backorder tracking, and backorder listing without breaking existing callers.
expectedOutcomes: OrderPriority is exported with standard and express values.
Order accepts an optional priority and defaults omitted priority to standard.
Invalid supplied priority values still raise OrderError.
reserveOrder records Backorder entries instead of throwing when stock is insufficient.
listBackorders returns every recorded Backorder.

children.title: Warehouse service backorders
children.objective: Expose backorder-aware warehouse operations and emit a warehouse event when a backorder is recorded.
expectedOutcomes: The service forwards the new domain behavior through its public operations.
A warehouse event is emitted for each recorded backorder.
Existing cancellation and reservation behavior remains available for orders with backorders.

children.title: Fulfillment wave priority
children.objective: Order express fulfillment before standard fulfillment within a wave without changing the planner signature.
expectedOutcomes: planFulfillment preserves its current call shape.
Within a single wave, express orders are planned before standard orders.
Existing wave behavior remains unchanged outside the priority ordering.

children.title: Durability backorder analytics
children.objective: Derive a backorders count in history analytics from the journaled events.
expectedOutcomes: HistoryAnalytics includes a backorders count.
The count is derived from recorded events rather than ad hoc state.
Existing journal history behavior stays intact.

children.title: API backorder surface
children.objective: Expose the current state's backorders through the server API.
expectedOutcomes: The server response includes the current state's backorders.
The API surface remains compatible with existing callers apart from the added backorder data.

children.title: Presentation express styling
children.objective: Distinguish express orders from standard orders in the rendered SVG.
expectedOutcomes: The tower SVG visually distinguishes express orders from standard orders.
The render remains stable for existing non-priority orders.

children.title: G6 probe stability
children.objective: Add the g6 probe and study:g6-probe script with deterministic single-object JSON output.
expectedOutcomes: src/probe/g6.ts exports main() returning a JSON string.
Direct invocation writes exactly one JSON object to stdout and nothing else.
Two runs from the same commit produce byte-identical output.
The package manifest exposes a study:g6-probe script.
